items.text:
Dinner Date is an experimental game, pushing at the edges of what a game can be. You play as Julian Luxemburg, a 27 year old British man who has been set up on a date with a 20 year old Japanese woman named Meiko. As the evening wears on, it becomes clear that Meiko will not be arriving for that date, leaving Julian alone with his thoughts. 

This is not a game with gameplay in the traditional sense. While the player can move Julian’s arms through a series of keyboard inputs and decide how much bread Julian eats or how much wine he drinks, none of these progress the gameplay in any way. The only progression through the game is the slow tick of the clock above the table and the meandering of Julian’s thoughts through possibilities, fears, and sorrow. 

It’s not a happy game in any way. It’s an experiential game, meant to convey a specific narrative and sensation of being engrossed in that narrative, and a way to experience an event in a safe and empathetic way. 

It’s in the assumptions this game makes about the universality of the experiences it depicts that I really struggled and why, perhaps, the game fell flat for me. Rather than empathising with Julian, I felt a softer version of what I felt when I played [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198031223198/recommended/520720/] Dear Esther. [/url] I felt unsafe, unclean, and grateful that Meiko never turned up to this unsettling evening.

In [url=https://www.npr.org/sections/alltechconsidered/2010/10/18/130646920/dinner-date] interviews [/url] he’s given about the game, Dinner Date’s creator, Jeroen Stout, described the game as an opportunity “to sympathize with someone who is slowly consumed by a sense of inadequacy” and a space to explore “things you can’t tell your friends.” This is fundamentally a game built around empathy and around having an unsafe experience in a safe space, and thus gaining a bit of empathy and a taste of the experience for oneself. Whether the game succeeds or fails at its goal is entirely contingent on well it builds the reality of the story and allows the player to inhabit this fundamentally unpleasant place. To be clear, with what little gameplay, graphics, and general interactivity Dinner Date has, it does a good job of drawing the player into the narrative. Throughout the game’s brief runtime, there is a decided sense of claustrophobia and anxiety as it becomes clear how much the player is trapped in this evening gone wrong. The glasses of wine and cigarettes only highlight the cycle of bad decisions that led to this point, and which will probably lead to more like it. 

As well as the game does with crafting a setting, though, what it didn’t succeed in doing was making me feel sympathy for Julian. Julian’s monologue about his life has the dual function of both creating a sense of anxiety and self-loathing, and telling a story - however brief - of who he is and how he got here. He talks about how he got to this point, his fears and doubts, and what he wanted with the evening. 

In doing so, this stopped being a game I could see myself in. Instead, I saw the mind of every man who has harassed me in the street, the ones who would not stop pestering me for my number, the ones who followed me home and made me feel unsafe. In listening to Julian’s monologue, I saw a bit more of the truths of the men who believed themselves to be entitled to  my company, and I did not sympathise with them. 

That Stout hopes Dinner Date captures some degree of universality and expects empathy worries me. 

It’s hard to put my finger on what exactly makes me uncomfortable about Julian Luxembourg. It may be that he is 27, waiting for a 20 year old woman to come into his apartment so he can have sex with her. It may be how he softly rages when she doesn’t appear, mentally accusing her of sleeping around. It may be the way he repeats that he “deserves” this over the course of the evening, though whether that “this” is the date or the sex is unclear. It may be the way he continues to sit at the table for hours, staring at the door after it’s long become apparent she’s not coming. It may be that he doesn’t call her and instead prefers to linger in the fantasies of what-ifs rather than engaging with her as a person. It’s this long medley of thoughts and actions that sent my hackles up and made me feel uncomfortable to be in this man’s skin. If there is a universality to his thoughts about being stood up, it’s not one I identify with. It’s entirely possible that universality is a male one, but even then, I would hate to believe that the universal male experience is to mentally slut shame a significantly younger woman for not coming to a late evening at an older man’s apartment. 

If the idea of the game is to make me feel empathy as a man spirals into self-loathing, it fails. I see the self-loathing, but the way it manifests is toxic. Self-loathing has a tendency towards toxicity, sure, but that toxicity isn’t inherently misogynistic. There are ways to tell this story that make it actually universal and actually generate some degree of empathy. The story told here is an explanation rather than an event. 

I think, too, this game hits a bit differently, given that I played it the day before getting stood up on a date of my own. It’s in the comparison of my experience and thoughts and Julian’s that the ideas and goals of this game ring truly hollow.

My potential date was meant to meet me for coffee. It was supposed to be the first date I’d been on in years. I went across the city to meet her, fiddling with my nails, my hair, my clothes, my phone on the metro the whole way. She e-mailed me as I was arriving at the coffee shop, telling me she wasn’t going to be able to make it, and I was left there, standing outside the coffee shop, unsure of what to do with my now empty afternoon. 

I got a cup of tea, sat down, and finished the book I’d been trying and failing to read on the metro. 

As I sat and read and drank my tea, I thought through the things that had brought me to that point. I thought about my nervousness about the date, and about the woman I was planning to meet. My mind ran back through all the things I’d planned to talk about, all the jokes I’d tell, and all the things I’d imagined she’d say that I would laugh at and sympathise with in turn. I played through the scenarios I’d imagined, then set them all aside. I did not know why she’d cancelled on me. I wasn’t going to ask because her business was her own. All that mattered was that there was no date, and it was up to me to decide how to move on from that. I could linger, and in so doing, accomplish nothing but misery for everyone, or I could go on with my life, and she hers.

I drank my tea. I went home. I moved on.

This story of my own date is not necessarily a better version of the story Stout chose to tell. However, that it’s a different story speaks volumes about the story he is telling, and about the ideas he believes are inherent. I recognise that my experience as a woman may colour my views on dating and male toxicity. That this is a game meant for men and the male dating experience, and I will therefore never actually be able to find myself in it is an entirely valid possibility. If that is the case, it works, and I humbly accept that, as a non-male, I do not have a clear window on the male experience.

However, if this is a game offering universality and a generally understandable portrait of empathy, it’s worth considering why it doesn’t work from my female perspective. In being locked in Julian’s narrative, I think of my own narrative and though processes. I compare our paths, and to compensate for my own failings, I critique his. I find him wanting, perhaps as a solace to myself, and perhaps as a subjective truth, but I find his is not a head I feel safe in. 

We can be sad. We can feel pain. It doesn’t have to be at the expense of others.

《晚餐约会》是一款实验性游戏，它不断推探游戏可能性的边界。你扮演朱利安·卢森堡，一个27岁的英国男人，被安排与一位名叫美子的20岁日本女性约会。随着夜晚流逝，越来越明显的是，美子不会来赴约，只留下朱利安独自面对自己的思绪。

这不是一款传统意义上的有玩法的游戏。虽然玩家可以通过一系列键盘输入来移动朱利安的手臂，决定朱利安吃多少面包或喝多少酒，但这些都不会以任何方式推进游戏进程。游戏中唯一的推进，是桌上时钟缓慢的滴答声，以及朱利安的思绪在种种可能性、恐惧与悲伤之间的游荡。

这绝不是一款快乐的游戏。它是一款体验式游戏，意在传达一段特定的叙事，以及沉浸于那段叙事中的感受，并提供一种以安全且富有同理心的方式去体验某个事件的方法。

正是在这款游戏对其所描绘经历的普遍性所作出的假设上，我真正感到了挣扎，也许这也是为什么这款游戏对我来说没有奏效。与其说我对朱利安产生了共情，不如说我感受到的，是我玩[url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198031223198/recommended/520720/]《亲爱的艾丝特》[/url]时所感受到的一种更温和版本。我感到不安全、不干净，并且庆幸美子从未出现在这个令人不安的夜晚。

在[url=https://www.npr.org/sections/alltechconsidered/2010/10/18/130646920/dinner-date]采访[/url]中，《晚餐约会》的创作者耶伦·斯托特谈到这款游戏时，将其描述为一个“去同情一个逐渐被自我不足感吞噬的人”的机会，以及一个探索“你无法告诉朋友的事情”的空间。从根本上说，这是一款围绕共情构建的游戏，也围绕在安全空间中经历一次不安全的体验，从而为自己获得一点共情和对那种体验的一丝品味。这款游戏在目标上是成功还是失败，完全取决于它多好地构建了故事的现实，并让玩家栖居在这个根本上令人不快的地方。需要明确的是，就《晚餐约会》所拥有的那点玩法、画面和一般互动性而言，它在把玩家拉入叙事方面做得不错。在游戏短暂的运行时间里，有一种明确的幽闭恐惧和焦虑感，因为玩家显然被困在这个出了错的夜晚里。那些酒杯和香烟只是突显了导致走到这一步的糟糕决定循环，而这种循环很可能还会导致更多类似的夜晚。

然而，尽管这款游戏在营造场景方面做得不错，它未能做到的是让我对朱利安产生同情。朱利安关于自己生活的独白具有双重功能：既制造焦虑和自我厌恶感，也讲述一个故事——无论多么简短——关于他是谁，以及他如何走到这里。他谈到自己如何走到这一步、他的恐惧和怀疑，以及他对这个夜晚的期待。

正因如此，这不再是一款我能从中看到自己的游戏。相反，我看到的是每一个在街上骚扰过我的男人的心灵，那些不停纠缠我要电话号码的人，那些跟着我回家并让我感到不安全的人。听着朱利安的独白，我更多看到的是那些自认为有权得到我陪伴的男人的一些真相，而我并不同情他们。

斯托特希望《晚餐约会》能捕捉某种程度的普遍性并期待共情，这让我担忧。

很难准确指出究竟是什么让我对朱利安·卢森堡感到不适。也许是因为他27岁，却等着一个20岁的女人来到他的公寓，好和她发生性关系。也许是因为当她没有出现时，他那种轻柔的愤怒，在心里指责她到处乱睡。也许是因为他整晚反复说自己“活该”如此，尽管这个“如此”指的是约会还是性并不清楚。也许是因为在早已明显她不会来之后，他仍继续在桌边坐上几个小时，盯着门口。也许是因为他不给她打电话，反而宁愿徘徊在种种“如果”的幻想中，而不是把她当作一个人来接触。正是这一长串思绪和行为的混合，让我警觉起来，并让我感到待在这个男人的皮囊里很不舒服。如果他对被放鸽子这件事的想法有什么普遍性，那也不是我认同的普遍性。完全有可能这种普遍性是男性的，但即便如此，我也不愿相信普遍的男性体验，是因为一个更年轻得多的女人没有来到一个年长男人的公寓参加深夜约会，就在心里荡妇羞辱她。

如果这款游戏的想法是在一个男人陷入自我厌恶时让我产生共情，那么它失败了。我看到了自我厌恶，但它表现的方式是有毒的。当然，自我厌恶往往趋向有毒，但这种毒性本身并不必然是厌女的。讲述这个故事有很多方式，可以让它真正具有普遍性，并真正产生某种程度的共情。这里讲述的故事是一种解释，而不是一个事件。

我也觉得，这款游戏给人的感受略有不同，因为我在自己约会被人放鸽子的前一天玩了它。正是在把我的经历和想法与朱利安的进行比较时，这款游戏的理念和目标才显得真正空洞。

我原本可能约会的对象本应和我一起喝咖啡。那本该是我多年来的第一次约会。我穿过整座城市去见她，一路上在地铁里摆弄我的指甲、头发、衣服和手机。就在我到达咖啡店时，她给我发了电子邮件，告诉我她来不了，于是我留在那里，站在咖啡店外，不知道该拿这个突然空下来的下午怎么办。

我买了一杯茶，坐下，读完了那本我在地铁上一直试图读却读不进去的书。

当我坐着读书喝茶时，我回想了一遍把我带到那一刻的种种事情。我想到了自己对这次约会的紧张，也想到了我打算见的那位女性。我的思绪回顾了所有我计划要谈的事情、所有我会讲的笑话，以及所有我想象中她会说的话，而我会依次报以大笑和共情。我在脑中演了一遍自己想象过的那些场景，然后把它们全都放到一边。我不知道她为什么取消。我不打算问，因为她的事是她自己的事。唯一重要的是没有约会了，而如何从中继续前行取决于我自己。我可以徘徊不去，并因此除了给每个人带来痛苦之外什么也得不到，也可以继续我的生活，而她也继续她的。

我喝完茶。我回家。我继续前行。

我自己这次约会的故事，未必是斯托特选择讲述的那个故事的更好版本。然而，它是一个不同的故事，这一点很能说明他所讲述的故事，以及他认为理所当然的那些观念。我承认，我作为女性的经历可能会影响我对约会和男性毒性的看法。这是一款为男人和男性约会体验而做的游戏，因此我将永远无法真正从中找到自己，这完全是一种可能。如果是这样，那么它奏效了，我谦卑地接受，作为一个非男性，我并没有一扇清晰观察男性体验的窗户。

然而，如果这是一款提供普遍性、并提供一幅大体可理解的共情画像的游戏，那么就值得思考为什么它从我的女性视角来看并不奏效。被困在朱利安的叙事中时，我想到了我自己的叙事和思维过程。我比较我们的道路，而为了补偿我自己的失败，我批判他的。我觉得他有所欠缺，也许这是对自己的安慰，也许这是主观真相，但我觉得他的脑袋不是一个让我感到安全的脑袋。

我们可以悲伤。我们可以感到痛苦。但这不必以他人为代价。
普遍性和期待共情让我担忧。

很难确切指出朱利安·卢森堡到底哪里让我不舒服。也许是因为他27岁，正等着一个20岁的女人走进他的公寓，好和她发生性关系。也许是因为当她没出现时，他那种轻柔的愤怒，在心里指责她到处乱搞。也许是因为他在整个晚上反复说自己“活该”这样，尽管这个“这样”指的是约会还是性爱并不清楚。也许是因为他继续在桌边坐上几个小时，在早已明显她不会来之后还盯着门口。也许是因为他不给她打电话，反而宁愿沉浸在种种假设的幻想中，而不是把她当作一个人来对待。正是这一长串的想法和行为让我毛骨悚然，让我在这个男人的皮囊里感到不舒服。如果他对被放鸽子的想法有什么普遍性，那也不是我能认同的。这种普遍性完全可能是男性的，但即便如此，我也不愿相信普遍的男性体验就是在心里荡妇羞辱一个比自己年轻得多的女人，只因为她没来赴一个年长男人公寓里的深夜之约。

如果这个游戏的意图是让我在一个男人陷入自我厌恶时感到共情，那它失败了。我看到了自我厌恶，但它表现的方式是有毒的。自我厌恶确实有走向有毒的倾向，但这种有毒并不必然带有厌女色彩。有办法讲述这个故事，让它真正具有普遍性，并真正产生某种程度的共情。这里讲述的故事是一种解释，而不是一个事件。

items.text:
How this even got an indie game award is beyond me...  This isn't a game.  It's as everyone else in the reviews say.  It's a guy coping with his thoughts on his expected date, as you make him eat infinite bread and wine.  

That's it...

This isn't a game.  It's a semi-interactive reddit post.
It's anything BUT a game.  There's no enjoyment to be had, there's no objective, there's no challenge, there's no freedom, there isn't even  a story!  It's a man giving monologue.  

I paid a dollar to hear a man monologue about nothing.  I expected nothing when I bought this on sale, and I'm still disappointed that I bought it.
items.text_zh:
这玩意儿居然还能拿独立游戏奖，我真是想不通……这不是游戏。就像评论里其他人说的那样。这是一个男人在应对自己对预期约会对象的想法，而你让他吃无限的面包和葡萄酒。

就这样……

这不是游戏。这是一篇半互动的Reddit帖子。
它唯独不是游戏。没有任何乐趣可言，没有目标，没有挑战，没有自由，甚至连故事都没有！就是一个男人在独白。

我花了一美元听一个男人对着一无所有的东西独白。我打折买这个的时候就没抱任何期望，但我还是后悔买了它。

items.text: This game sucks. There is no point in playing due to the fact that it is just random movements and a guy talking to himself. It lasts 5 minutes and there is no real context to the story line. It is just a guy that gets stood up on a dinner date and drinks some wine alone. I wouldn't play it if I was paid to.

items.text:
Yeah, it's bad. 

It's the clear result of an inability to either write a short story or make a video game, so instead you get a half-baked 'narrative' with no actual gameplay to speak of. Oh he got stood up, that's the end of that arc, oh you can look at the stuff in the room, that's the end of the game.

I can't emphasize how bad it is. I'm reviewing this years after I played it and I still feel completely burned by the purchase. Please, don't buy this game, don't get conned like I did.

items.text:
This was an experience really destroyed by having any expectations and paying money.

I went into it really happy to see something like this, but man did it fall short. It is about 15 minutes long and there's basically nothing to do or affect. The subject matter was so banal that I spent the whole time waiting for a breaththrough that just doesn't happen.

I think it is also misleading by saying you "become the subconscious" of the main character. Because you don't, you just hear it, and the only think you control is some conscious decision making (like pouring wine) and order of operations. In that way, it's a kind of interesting slightly experimental movie, but it's far from any roleplay possibilities offered by using a videogame over a short film.

I did like a lot of the visual design. The objects were well designed and the icons conveyed their points well while working with the theme. The acting was good.

I really wanted to like it. I think it's an interesting portfolio piece for all involved. But it's not worth paying for.

这本来是一次被任何期望和花钱彻底毁掉的体验。

我进去的时候真的很高兴能看到这样的东西，但天哪，它差得太远了。它大约15分钟长，基本上没有什么可做或可影响的。题材如此平庸，以至于我全程都在等待一个根本不会发生的突破。

我觉得说你会“成为主角的潜意识”也是误导。因为你并没有，你只是听到它，你唯一能控制的就是一些有意识的决策（比如倒酒）和操作顺序。那样的话，它算是一种有点意思、略微实验性的电影，但远不及使用电子游戏而非短片所能提供的任何角色扮演可能性。

我确实喜欢很多视觉设计。物品设计得很好，图标在配合主题的同时很好地传达了它们的含义。表演也不错。

我真的很想喜欢它。我认为对所有参与者来说，这是一件有趣的 portfolio 作品。但它不值得花钱。

Mai giocato un gioco più noioso di questo, e dire che ho giocato a The Graveyard.
Tipico esperimento/gioco/progetto/idea artistica che cerca di darti un messaggio, ma che alla fine ti fà annoiare.
Dinner Date è fra i peggiori che ho provato.
La trama del gioco è semplicemente aspettare una ragazza a casa tua per un appuntamento di cui vi siete dati. E basta, la trama è tutto qui, lei gli tira il pacco e lui si fà tantissime seghe mentali sul perchè nessuno vuole uscire con lui, sul perchè i suoi amici scopano e lui no, e mille altri pensieri di questo tipo. [b]Seriamente, perchè dovrebbe interessarmi una trama di questo tipo?[/b] è solo un tizio che pensa a mille cose "uhhh chissà cosa farà tizio, uhhh chissà cosa fara caio uhhhh quella che mi ha tirato il pacco e una troia, buhuhu sono molto triste , voglio strapparmi le orecchie, ma non posso :cccc"
Niente di interessante, non mi ha lasciato nessun tipo di messaggio particolare, non ha neanche lasciato nessun tipo di esperienza videoludica. 

[h1]PRO[/h1]
..... i suoni?

[h1]CONTRO[/h1]
-3 euro, seriamente? manco gratis lo consiglio
-Classico "gioco" dove di "gioco" non ha nulla. 
-Non ci sono cose che ti fanno riflettere [spoiler](se vuoi stare in compagnia con amici o scopare con ragazze, devi uscire di casa, WOW CHE FINALE! WOW QUANTE EMOZIONI! WOW, QUANTO TUTTO!')[/spoiler]

items.text:
Playing this game is like reading this review. You don't have any real control over this situation except for your ability to say: "Stuff it. I'm going to do something else.", stop reading and close the window.

 Now, I'm just going to sit here for a bit until you move the mouse into the right position for me to finish writing the rest of the review. I know that feels fruitless because you aren't helping dictate the outcome of the review in any way, but your time has already been wasted, so you might as well see what happens...

 Seriously though, a game that focuses on story and character is fine, but the story and character have to be interesting and compelling. Eating bread and thinking about how much you must suck to get stood up?... Doesn't cut it. We have no agency in the game or story which makes the requirement of "pick up bread" and "pour yourself some wine" little more than a "click to read the next paragraph" button.

 Conflict is the essence of drama, but the only conflict here will be the struggle to decide if the effort required is worth it to get your $3 back.

Normally I actually enjoy games like these. Games where not much happens. Games without enemies where you just explore.
This can't even be called a 'walking simulator'. It's a nothing simulator. For me, it wasn't thought-provoking or moving or even interesting, like most of these types of games aim to be in place of traditional gameplay. If you're going to remove gameplay elements like combat, leveling, etc you need to replace with them *something*. A story is usually what developers go with. Here they decided to go in a much more experimental direction and just replace all gameplay elements - including story - with nothing.
Also, the game is incredibly short (this might be good, though). The time that I have on record is exactly how long it took me to complete the 'story' without rushing.
This should have been a free game and even then it would have been hard to recommend.
items.text_zh:
通常我其实很喜欢这类游戏。那些没什么事情发生的游戏。没有敌人、你只是探索的游戏。
这甚至不能被称为“步行模拟器”。它是一个虚无模拟器。对我来说，它并不发人深省，也不感人，甚至不有趣，而大多数这类游戏都旨在用这些来替代传统玩法。如果你要移除战斗、升级等玩法元素，你需要用*某些东西*来替代它们。故事通常是开发者选择的东西。在这里，他们决定走向一个更加实验性的方向，把所有玩法元素——包括故事——都替换成了虚无。
另外，这个游戏短得令人难以置信（不过这可能也是好事）。我记录的时间正好就是我不赶时间完成“故事”所花的时间。
这本来应该是一个免费游戏，即便如此也很难推荐。

items.text:
Dinner Date is a first person experience that puts you into someone's subconscious. You'll see what he sees and hear his thoughts as he waits for his date and you'll push keys. The key prompts float in little bubbles that have hints about what they'll do. Different keys do different things. You'll get to pour a glass of wine, look at the clock, check your left hand and gaze at your right hand. There are even such details like putting your spoon into soup, stirring it, put the spoon back down and so on. You'll hear the character talk, basically telling you which of the things to do next.

Going into the game I thought it would be another 'crazy hand simulator' like Surgeon Simulator or Ampu-Tea. Nope, you just press keys to do things when the prompts are up.

You have no control over movement or the camera, just over what the character does as he continues to worry about his date. He will wonder whether to drink another glass of wine and what else he could be doing. The dinner date is a quick experience, over in about 30 minutes. Trying to replay it again didn't lead me to think that there are different outcomes.

Dinner Date has a lot going for it, the voice acting is good, the environment is great, but its just a small kitchen with a table in it. You'll go to the window to have a cigarette, but that's it. This could be the demo of a bigger more detailed game, there is talent here, but I just didn't have fun playing the game. Plus there's not much here to get excited about. Its over quick. If a bobbing camera gets you motion sick, avoid this game.

Here's something to think about when telling a story. If its not the most interesting thing that happens to the character,  why aren't you telling the more interesting story? Is it technical limitations such as having characters to interact with? Is this what leads the character up to his suicide or finding his true love after the game has ended? Is it witty banter amongst two characters blended with subconscious thought? No, but maybe that will happen in Dinner Date 2: The Reckoning. I'm sure that Luke Skywalker had moments where he just chilled in his bedroom thinking about a girl. That never made it into Star Wars.

Dinner Date was just watching something while I mash all keys at once since there's no sort of right or wrong. Other narrative experiences like Dear Esther and Gone Home at least give you movement control and environments to explore. Like the plot of Dinner Date, it stands in a category all its own.
items.text_zh:
《晚餐约会》是一款第一人称体验，将你带入某人的潜意识。当他等待约会对象时，你会看到他所看到的，听到他的想法，而你要按键。按键提示漂浮在小气泡中，气泡里带有关于它们会做什么的提示。不同的键做不同的事。你将有机会倒一杯酒、看时钟、检查左手并凝视右手。甚至还有这样的细节，比如把勺子放进汤里、搅拌、把勺子放回去等等。你会听到角色说话，基本上是在告诉你接下来该做哪些事。

进入游戏前，我以为这会是另一款像《外科医生模拟》或《Ampu-Tea》那样的“疯狂手部模拟器”。不，你只是在提示出现时按键来做事情。

你无法控制移动或镜头，只能控制角色在继续担心约会时做什么。他会犹豫是否再喝一杯酒，以及自己还能做些什么。晚餐约会是一次很短的体验，大约30分钟就结束了。尝试再玩一遍并没有让我觉得会有不同结果。

《晚餐约会》有很多优点，配音很好，环境很棒，但它只是一个带桌子的小厨房。你会走到窗边抽根烟，但也就这样了。这可能是某个更大、更细致游戏的试玩版，这里有才华，但我玩这个游戏就是没觉得有趣。另外，这里也没什么值得兴奋的内容。它很快就结束了。如果晃动的镜头会让你晕动，避开这个游戏。

讲故事时，有件事值得思考。如果这不是角色身上发生的最有趣的事，那你为什么不讲那个更有趣的故事？是技术限制，比如必须有可互动的角色吗？这是否导致角色在游戏结束后走向自杀或找到真爱？是两个角色之间机智的斗嘴与潜意识思绪交织吗？不，但也许那会发生在《晚餐约会2：清算》里。我确信卢克·天行者也有过只是待在自己卧室里想着一个女孩的时刻。那从没被拍进《星球大战》。

《晚餐约会》只是在我同时乱按所有键时看着某件事发生，因为根本没有什么对或错。像《亲爱的艾丝特》和《到家》这样的其他叙事体验，至少给你移动控制和可探索的环境。就像《晚餐约会》的剧情一样，它自成一类。

A idéia é boa. Mas somente a idéia, pois a execução é uma porcaria.

Achei realmente muito bacana esse lance de controlar as reações do personagem, em ser o subconciente dele, no entanto a história é ruim pra caramba: você controla as reações de um cara que levou um bolo num jantar à dois e é obrigado a ouvir ele se lamentar e formular idéia sobre o motivo pelo qual levou o bolo.

Sinceramente... Já me cançam os ouvidos ter que ouvir os lamentos de dor-de-cotovelo das pessoas ao redor... ter que aturar "choramingos" em um jogo eletrônico é não dá. Talvez fosse melhor se o jogo fosse mais poético (seilá), mas na verdade é só "sofrença" o tempo inteiro.

Costumo gostar bastante de jogos artítiscos, mas este não vale a pena.

我通常挺喜欢艺术游戏的，但这个不值得。

items.text:
Usually I really love artistic games and I really like the idea for this game. I also rarely wish I could refund a game I've bought from Steam, even if I dislike it. This is not one of those times. 2.99 is actually way too much for such a lack of game.

Positive things first:
 - I actually did like the monologue and felt badly for the character, pathetic as he was. However, my dislike for the character rose as I realized that my actions did not have any effect on him.
 - ...it's cheap?

Negative things:

 - I don't know about anyone else, but my subconcious desires and fears do have some effect on my life, besides where I look. In fact, that is an incredibly random thing for a "sub-concious" to control. Looking back at the description of the game, I think it should be more evident that the point of the game is not to "play" but to listen. I wouldn't be interested in such a game, but I think they could have avoided a lot of alienation but spelling it out that this was a game like Dear Esther. There is obviously an aundience for this type of game, this really should be described better for this crowd.

 - Again, looking back at the description, I see a lot of "unanswered question" type wonderings, but the game is rather straightforword. Julian does not like his coworkers. He does like Byron. There is no real reason to play after the first "act", because it is all spelled out there. I criticized its lousy gameplay strategy before but now I'm criticizing its storytelling.
   
   Why should I care about Julian? Yes, it sucks that he got stood up, but so what? There is no mystery to him, which is fine in real life, but characters who spend 20 minutes or so talking about themselves should really have something interesting to say. Sure, he likes poetry, but so do a lot of people. And they are probably less insufferable and boring than Julian is. No new information is gathered in each subsequent act and there is no real reason to have the game continue with no new information or insight.

   The game's story got ever-so-slightly more interesting near the end, when someone knocks at the door, and I did feel something at his emotions afterward, but that really doesn't excuse the 20 minutes of boredom proceeding that. Boredom can be used in video games and stories, but it should be rewarded or serve a point.

So, no, I would not recommend this game to anyone. It is not a game, it is not a compelling story, and it isn't even a good sleep aid, since no one could sleep over Julian's whining.

通常我真的很喜欢艺术性游戏，而且我真的很喜欢这个游戏的点子。我也很少希望自己能退款一个从Steam买的游戏，即使我不喜欢它。这次不是那种时候。2.99对于如此缺乏游戏性的东西来说，实际上太贵了。

先说优点：
 - 我其实确实喜欢那段独白，也为这个角色感到难过，尽管他很可悲。然而，当我意识到我的行为对他没有任何影响时，我对这个角色的反感增加了。
 - ……它很便宜？

缺点：

 - 我不知道别人怎么样，但我的潜意识欲望和恐惧确实对我的生活有一些影响，除了我看向哪里。事实上，对于一个“潜意识”来说，控制这个是非常随机的事情。回头看游戏的描述，我觉得应该更明显地表明，这个游戏的重点不是“玩”，而是倾听。我不会对这样的游戏感兴趣，但我认为他们本可以避免很多疏离感，只要明确说明这是一个像《亲爱的艾丝特》那样的游戏。显然这类游戏有受众，这真的应该为这类人群描述得更好。

 - 再次回头看描述，我看到很多“未解问题”式的疑惑，但游戏其实相当直白。朱利安不喜欢他的同事。他确实喜欢拜伦。在第一“幕”之后，没有真正的理由继续玩，因为一切都在那里说明白了。我之前批评过它糟糕的游戏玩法策略，但现在我在批评它的叙事。
   
   我为什么要关心朱利安？是的，他被放鸽子了很糟糕，但那又怎样？他身上没有谜团，这在现实生活中没问题，但一个花20分钟左右谈论自己的角色，真的应该有一些有趣的东西可说。当然，他喜欢诗歌，但很多人也喜欢。而且他们可能没有朱利安那么令人难以忍受和无聊。在随后的每一幕中都没有收集到新信息，也没有真正的理由让游戏在没有新信息或洞见的情况下继续下去。

   游戏的故事在接近结尾时变得稍微有趣了一点，当时有人敲门，之后我确实对他的情绪有所感触，但这真的不能为之前20分钟的无聊开脱。无聊可以在电子游戏和故事中使用，但它应该得到回报或服务于某个目的。

所以，不，我不会向任何人推荐这个游戏。它不是游戏，不是引人入胜的故事，甚至不是好的助眠工具，因为没人能在朱利安的抱怨声中睡着。

items.text:
[b]Персональный рейтинг - 3 из 10[/b]

- Алло...
- Петя? Это Маша. Ты придешь на День Рождения Оксаны?
- К этой гадине?! После того, как она поступила со мной? Она путалась со всеми вокруг. Я застал ее как она кувыркалась с моим лучшим другом, представляешь? То есть, теперь уже бывшим лучшим другом... 
- Зачем же так грубо? Может, она хочет попросить прощения! Она сказала, что очень хочет видеть тебя на своем празднике, даже подарка не надо.
- Ишь хитрая какая. Я ей не верю... Здесь что-то не так, она наверняка захочет выставить меня дураком!
- Слушай, если перестанешь доверять девушкам, то так и останешься один!
- Ладно, ладно... Уговорила. Но мне совсем нечего надеть... Я пролил кетчуп на мои парадные штаны и теперь они все грязные...
- Ты что, на прием к президенту идешь? Накинь свои фирменные шорты и кроссовки, ты без них никуда...
- Хм. Или, может, одеть отцовский пиджак с бабочкой... Вот все обзавидуются!

Приблизительно такой диалог в общем-то без начала и конца пришел на ум после 15 минут игры в Dinner Date. Да, игра длится порядка 15 минут... 

Такие игры как Dinner Date, формально, и не игры вовсе, а некий сеанс психоанализа в рамках отдельно взятой истории. Это своеобразный психологический очерк, уступающий место рефлексии и прочим терминам из прикладной психологии. Все зависит от вас и лично вашего восприятия. Кто-то найдет в психологическом портрете героя отражение самого себя, кому-то покажется знакомой его история, а меланхолично-ненавязчивый саундтрек лишь подчеркнет основные элементы повествования и заставит мозг как следует пробежаться по темным уголкам вашего подсознания и, словно с пыльного чердака, стащить оттуда те воспоминания, о которых вспоминать не принято.  

Порой кажется, что подобные произведения созданы исключительно для одного единственного человека - автора этих самых произведений. Отчасти это здравый подход. Как в арт-хаусном кино: авторский стиль, своеобразная манера подачи, истории без начала и конца - разобраться в хитросплетениях и собрать паззл воедино смогут единицы. В противном случае, высок риск запутаться в образах и метафорах, словно в паутине. И единственным вопросом после прохождения будет являться лишь "Что это было?".
items.text_zh:
[b]个人评分 - 10分中的3分[/b]

- 喂……
- 佩佳？我是玛莎。你会来参加奥克萨娜的生日吗？
- 去那个贱人那儿？！在她那样对我之后？她跟周围所有人都乱搞。我撞见她跟我的最好的朋友滚在一起，你能想象吗？也就是说，现在是前最好的朋友了……
- 何必这么粗鲁？也许她想请求原谅！她说她非常想在她的庆祝会上见到你，甚至不需要礼物。
- 哟，真狡猾。我不信她……这里有点不对劲，她肯定会想让我出丑！
- 听着，如果你不再信任女孩，那你就只能一直单身了！
- 好吧，好吧……你说服我了。但我完全没衣服穿……我把番茄酱洒在我的礼服裤子上了，现在它们全脏了……
- 你是要去见总统吗？套上你的招牌短裤和运动鞋吧，你离不开它们……
- 嗯。或者，也许穿父亲的西装外套配蝴蝶结……那样所有人都会羡慕！

大致上就是这样一个没有开头也没有结尾的对话，在玩了《Dinner Date》15分钟后浮现在脑海中。是的，游戏大约持续15分钟……

像《Dinner Date》这样的游戏，形式上根本不是游戏，而是在一个单独故事框架内的一种心理分析疗程。这是一篇独特的心理随笔，让位给反思以及应用心理学中的其他术语。一切都取决于你和你个人的感知。有人会在主角的心理画像中找到自己的倒影，有人会觉得他的故事很熟悉，而忧郁而不张扬的配乐只会强调叙事的基本元素，迫使大脑好好跑一遍你潜意识的黑暗角落，并像从积满灰尘的阁楼里一样，从那里拖出那些不习惯回忆的记忆。

有时似乎这类作品只为一个唯一的人创作——这些作品本身的作者。部分来说这是合理的做法。就像在艺术电影中：作者风格、独特的呈现方式、没有开头和结尾的故事——能理清错综复杂之处并把拼图拼凑完整的人寥寥无几。否则，就很有可能像在蜘蛛网中一样迷失在形象和隐喻里。而通关后唯一的问题只会是“这是什么？”

observations.description: 故事没有开头和结尾
observations.evidence: без начала и конца
observations.evidence_zh: 没有开头也没有结尾

items.text:
Dinner Date is about a man who is getting stood up and watch him eat dinner, look at the clock, stir his soup around and even talk to himself about....stuff. 

Now I'm use to these sort of 'artistic' games since Dear Esther is one of my fav indie games but in that game you can move freely and look at what ever you want, Dinner Date on the other hand doesn't let you.For most of the game you pretty much sit at the table and tell him what to do. They do not give you the ability to give you the control over him at all, instead they let you select what to do with floating bubbles that tell you want to press. 

Want to stir your soup around? there's a button for that!

Want to eat some bread? There's a button for that!

Want to look at what time it is? They got a button for that to!

I guess what they tried to do to make this game appealing to people is what the character is going through by making you listen to everything he says as time passes by but even that falls flat after listening to him complain and talk about getting laid, ya it goes there oddly and near the end it just gets weird. 

Oddly enough tho I actually thought about how this 'game' could be allot better if done right and it pretty much came down to not making it into a game. This 'game' should not have been turned into.....what ever you want to call this since clearly I'm not calling it a game anymore, and instead they should have turned it into a short film. This could have been a perfect little project for someone who had the time to write the script, strap a GoPro Hero on to there face and went go with it.

With that said, I will rate this game a simple 2/10.

《晚餐约会》讲的是一个男人被人放了鸽子，然后你看着他吃晚饭、看时钟、搅动他的汤，甚至自言自语地聊些……东西。

现在我已经习惯了这类“艺术”游戏，因为《亲爱的艾丝特》是我最喜欢的独立游戏之一，但在那款游戏里你可以自由移动，想看什么就看什么，而《晚餐约会》则不然。游戏的大部分时间里，你基本上就是坐在桌边，告诉他该做什么。他们根本没有给你控制他的能力，而是让你通过漂浮的气泡来选择该做什么，气泡会告诉你按什么键。

想把汤搅一搅？有个按钮可以做到！

想吃点面包？有个按钮可以做到！

想看看现在几点了？他们也有个按钮可以做到！

我猜他们为了让这款游戏对人们有吸引力，试图做的就是让你随着时间流逝听他说的每一句话，从而体会角色所经历的一切，但即便是这一点，在听他抱怨、谈论上床之后也变得索然无味了，是的，它奇怪地扯到了那上面，而且快到结尾时它就变得很诡异。

不过奇怪的是，我居然真的想过，如果做得好，这个“游戏”本可以好得多，而结论基本上就是：别把它做成游戏。这个“游戏”本不该被变成……随便你怎么称呼它吧，因为显然我已经不再叫它游戏了，相反，他们本该把它拍成一部短片。对于有时间写剧本、在脸上绑一台GoPro Hero然后开拍的人来说，这本来可以是个完美的小项目。

话虽如此，我会给这款游戏简单地打2/10分。

Este "juego" tiene varios problemas.

1.- No es juego. Al menos no en el sentido que alguna de las "decisiones" que uno tome puedan tener algún impacto en el final (o en algún momento). Puedes intentar tomarte un litro de vino sin que algo cambie (y de hecho, la botella ni siquiera cambia). El protagonista habla aún mientras estés comiendo, fumando o bebiendo... too much.

2.- Es aburrido. Así de simple, por último que la historia tuviera alguna suerte de profundidad.

3.- No tiene rejugabilidad. Si ya viste una vez cerca de 25 minutos, ¿tiene algún sentido ver exactamente lo mismo? Al menos si el punto 2 no fuera cierto, podría ser interesante 

4.- La descripción (ahora mirando con calma) describe exactamente lo que trata, pero la verdad es que no lo parece y eso es francamente intolerable.

En fin, nadie merece este juego, ni como un "demo" de algo que podría ser importante vale la pena. No, gratis tampoco. Son 25 minutos que puedes ver un capítulo de The Big Bang Theory o Friends.
items.text_zh:
这个“游戏”有几个问题。

1.- 它不是游戏。至少不是在你所做的任何“决定”能对结局（或在任何时候）产生某种影响的意义上。你可以试着喝下一升葡萄酒，什么都不会改变（事实上，连瓶子都不会变）。即使你在吃东西、抽烟或喝酒，主角也还在说话……太过分了。

2.- 它很无聊。就这么简单，至少如果故事能有某种深度的话。

3.- 它没有重玩价值。如果你已经看过一次大约25分钟的内容，再看完全一样的东西有什么意义吗？至少如果第2点不成立的话，可能会有点意思

4.- 描述（现在冷静地看）准确地描述了它讲的是什么，但事实是它看起来并不像，这实在令人无法忍受。

总之，没人配得上这个游戏，即使作为某个可能很重要的东西的“试玩版”也不值得。不，免费也不值。这25分钟你可以去看一集《生活大爆炸》或《老友记》。

items.text: I would not recommend this game to anyone except those looking to watch someone else explore the psychological underpinings of one man's night in. It was boring, the gameplay was limited, and even the psychological exploration was limited. I was excited about this one, but ultimately I left disapointed.

items.text:
A good start, but it lacked a climax. The story felt like it was just getting started 20 minutes in and then all of a sudden the credits rolled. 
The idea of not having major choices while making little ones is certainly interesting but there was no pay off.
Graphics are good, music is stellar, story was disappointing at best. 
The only thing this game accomplished was making me want some vegetable soup.

不做重大选择而只做小选择的想法当然很有趣，但没有任何回报。
画面不错，音乐很棒，故事充其量令人失望。
这款游戏唯一做到的事，就是让我想吃点蔬菜汤。

items.text: I'm sure this "game" will spur a lot of discussion about what a game is and whatnot... All that aside, I have to warn you and say that it's only about 22ish minutes long, and there's really no value in replaying. Mosly what one does during this 22 minute spiel is sitting through the narrator's story, and I do know that people have problems with that. There's minimal interaction with certain items, and that is done through pressing certain keys. Now, saying all that, I don't think the story is anything to write home about, and that is the main weakness of this game. I wouldn't really recommend it.
items.text_zh: 我确信这个“游戏”会引发很多关于什么才算游戏的讨论之类的……撇开所有这些不谈，我必须警告你并告诉你，它只有大约22分钟左右，而且重玩真的没有任何价值。在这22分钟的长篇大论中，人们主要做的就是坐着听完叙述者的故事，而我知道人们对这一点有意见。与某些物品有极少的互动，而且是通过按某些键来完成的。现在，说了这些之后，我认为这个故事没什么值得大书特书的，而这正是这款游戏的主要弱点。我不会真的推荐它。

items.text: Do not buy. This is not a pick your own adventure, this is not a game. It is about 30 minutes long, you play as a dude talking to himself. Did I say play, sorry I mean watching a loser be lonely and depress for 30 minutes. Game over. Worse of all the story is so lame and pathetic. I got it for 50 cents. And it is still not worth it. Don't get this game unless the developer pay you to play it.

items.text:
Do NOT buy this. Ever. I would go so far as to say that you shouldn't even play it if they offer it for free. It isn't a game. There's nothing of consequence to DO during the 15 minute movie. You can choose to dip your bread in sauce or just eat it plain, all while listening to some whiny ♥♥♥♥ complain about relationships and how hard it is to find love (or some such rubbish).

Not a game. Actually a piss-poor time-suck of a movie with a crappy character, bad dialogue, and a weak plot.

items.text:
In this high-budget blockbuster, you play as Dennis "Dinner" Dateman, as he attempts to beat the world record for self-pity. Featuring deep characterization (he wants to bang Japanese girls, and is uncompromising on this stance, as well as very vocal about it) a plot filled with twists and turns (Will the Japanese girl show up? Will he resist the urge to get drunk and have a breakdown about poetry? (No)) and a complex combo system (You can dip your bread in your soup OR in the dip, or even not dip it at all) this game is sure to have something for everyone. Don't miss out on the thrilling final act, in which he spends several minutes staring at the Dinosaur Comic on his fridge while throwing a tantrum about not remembering a poem.

Fedora DLC sold seperately.
items.text_zh:
在这部高预算大片中，你扮演丹尼斯·“晚餐”·戴特曼，他试图打破自怜的世界纪录。本作拥有深刻的人物塑造（他想上日本女孩，而且在这个立场上毫不妥协，还对此非常大声）一个充满转折的情节（日本女孩会出现吗？他能忍住不喝醉并因为诗歌而崩溃吗？（不能））以及复杂的连击系统（你可以把面包蘸进汤里，或者蘸进蘸料里，甚至完全不蘸），这款游戏肯定能满足每个人。不要错过激动人心的最后一幕，他会花好几分钟盯着冰箱上的《恐龙漫画》，同时因为记不住一首诗而大发脾气。

软呢帽DLC单独出售。
